questions.title: E-commerce Product Search
questions.scenario:
Database: retail_db | Collection: db.products | Field(s): ['category', 'stock']
You need to retrieve all documents from the products collection that belong to the 'electronics' category and have more than 0 items in stock.
questions.explanation: The find method uses a filter object where multiple fields imply a logical AND; $gt is the operator for 'greater than'.
questions.misconception: Users often forget that numeric comparisons require operators like $gt rather than simple assignment.

questions.title: IoT Sensor Data Insertion
questions.scenario:
Database: smart_home_db | Collection: db.climate_logs | Field(s): ['deviceId', 'temp']
A new temperature reading of 22.5 degrees has arrived from device 'living-room-01'. Which command correctly adds this single document?
questions.explanation: insertOne() is the standard MongoDB method for adding a single document to a collection.
questions.misconception: Users coming from SQL might look for 'INSERT INTO' equivalents like add() or push().

questions.title: Fintech Balance Increment
questions.scenario:
Database: banking_db | Collection: db.accounts | Field(s): ['accountHolder', 'balance']
An interest payment needs to be added to a customer's account. Increase the balance of 'Alice Smith' by exactly 5.50.
questions.explanation: The $inc operator is used to increment a numeric field by a specified value without overwriting the entire document.
questions.misconception: Beginners often try to use $set to add values instead of the $inc operator.

questions.title: SaaS User Projection
questions.scenario:
Database: saas_platform | Collection: db.users | Field(s): ['email', 'lastLogin']
You want to list all users but only return the 'email' field and the internal '_id' field for each document to save bandwidth.
questions.explanation: The second argument of find() is the projection object where '1' includes a field. _id is included by default.
questions.misconception: Novices often forget the empty filter braces {} and put the projection as the first argument.

questions.title: Gaming Profile Deletion
questions.scenario:
Database: gaming_zone | Collection: db.profiles | Field(s): ['isGuest', 'inactiveDays']
To free up space, delete all documents where the 'isGuest' field is set to true.
questions.explanation: deleteMany() removes all documents that match the filter criteria.
questions.misconception: deleteOne() might be used by mistake, which would only remove the first matching guest profile found.

questions.title: Fintech Transaction Audit Query
questions.scenario:
Database: fintech_db | Collection: db.transactions | Field(s): amount, status
Find all pending transactions with an amount strictly greater than 10000, projecting only the amount and status fields while suppressing the _id field.
questions.explanation: The query applies filtering criteria using the $gt operator and uses projection to explicitly include amount and status while omitting _id.
questions.misconception: Developers often forget that _id is included by default unless explicitly disabled with _id: 0.

questions.title: IoT Telemetry Temperature Alert Update
questions.scenario:
Database: iot_db | Collection: db.sensor_readings | Field(s): temperature, isFlagged
Update all sensor documents where temperature exceeds 85.0 to set isFlagged to true and record a new field alertTimestamp with the current date.
questions.expectedCommand: db.sensor_readings.updateMany({ temperature: { $gt: 85.0 } }, { $set: { isFlagged: true }, $currentDate: { alertTimestamp: true } })
questions.explanation: updateMany modifies all matching documents, using $set for boolean flags and $currentDate to efficiently assign timestamps without client clock drift.
questions.misconception: Using new Date() inside updates can introduce slight discrepancies across distributed application instances compared to $currentDate.

questions.title: E-commerce Inventory Array Filtering
questions.scenario:
Database: ecommerce_db | Collection: db.products | Field(s): tags, price
A merchant needs to retrieve products that contain both 'organic' and 'bulk' tags, regardless of order, and have a price under 50.
questions.explanation: The $all operator matches arrays that contain all specified elements irrespective of array order.
questions.misconception: Exact array matching db.products.find({ tags: ['organic', 'bulk'] }) requires exact ordering and identical length.

questions.title: Educational Portal Course Capacity Increment
questions.scenario:
Database: school_db | Collection: db.courses | Field(s): enrolledCount, capacity
Atomically increment the enrolledCount by 1 for courseCode 'CS101', but only if enrolledCount is strictly less than the capacity field.
questions.explanation: The $expr operator allows comparing two fields from the same document in a query filter, combined with $inc for concurrency-safe updates.
questions.misconception: Standard comparison operators like $lt cannot compare two fields directly without using $expr.

questions.title: Hospital Bed Occupancy Array Manipulation
questions.scenario:
Database: hospital_db | Collection: db.wards | Field(s): occupiedBeds, floor
Which operation removes the bed number 'B-104' from the occupiedBeds array for ward 'ICU-North' on floor 3?
questions.explanation: $pull removes all instances of a value or matching criteria from an array, whereas $pop removes only from the first or last index.
questions.misconception: $pop only takes 1 or -1 to specify removal by position, not by value.

questions.title: Hospital Patient Records Retrieval
questions.scenario:
Database: hospital_db | Collection: db.patients | Field(s): ['age', 'status']
A healthcare administrator needs to retrieve all patient documents where the age is exactly 75 and the status is 'admitted'.
questions.explanation: The find() method takes a query object where multiple fields imply a logical AND.
questions.misconception: Learners often forget that MongoDB field names are case-sensitive.

questions.title: Logistics Vehicle Tracking
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_db | Collection: db.fleet | Field(s): ['fuelLevel']
A fleet manager wants to count how many vehicles have a 'fuelLevel' strictly greater than 20 percent.
questions.explanation: The $gt operator selects documents where the value of the field is greater than the specified value.
questions.misconception: Users might try to use standard SQL comparison symbols like > directly in the query object.

questions.title: Social Media Profile Update
questions.scenario:
Database: social_db | Collection: db.profiles | Field(s): ['isPublic']
A user wants to set their 'isPublic' boolean field to false for their specific document identified by username 'jdoe123'.
questions.explanation: The $set operator replaces the value of a field with the specified value.
questions.misconception: Forgetting the $set operator will overwrite the entire document with just the new field.

questions.title: E-commerce Warehouse Stocking
questions.scenario:
Database: warehouse_db | Collection: db.inventory | Field(s): ['sku', 'tags']
A warehouse system needs to add a new item to the collection with a stock keeping unit 'SKU-99' and an array of tags ['shelf-A', 'perishable'].
questions.explanation: The insertOne() method is the standard way to add a single BSON document to a collection.
questions.misconception: New users might confuse the collection name with a table and try to use SQL-like 'ADD' commands.

questions.title: EdTech Course Sorting
questions.scenario:
Database: school_db | Collection: db.courses | Field(s): ['credits']
A registrar needs to see all courses sorted by the 'credits' field in descending order (highest credits first).
questions.explanation: In a sort() call, 1 indicates ascending order and -1 indicates descending order.
questions.misconception: Learners often mix up 1 and -1, thinking 1 means 'first' or 'highest'.

questions.title: Logistics Waypoint Status Push
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_db | Collection: db.shipments | Field(s): trackingNumber, checkpoints
A logistics dispatcher needs to append a new checkpoint location 'Distribution Center Dallas' with a timestamp to an in-transit parcel matching trackingNumber 'TRK-984210'.
questions.expectedCommand: db.shipments.updateOne({ trackingNumber: 'TRK-984210' }, { $push: { checkpoints: { location: 'Distribution Center Dallas', timestamp: new Date() } } })
acceptableAlternatives: db.shipments.updateOne({trackingNumber: "TRK-984210"}, {$push: {checkpoints: {location: "Distribution Center Dallas", timestamp: new Date()}}})
questions.explanation: The $push operator appends a specified value or subdocument to an existing array field in MongoDB.
questions.misconception: Using $set instead of $push will overwrite the entire array instead of appending an element.

questions.title: Gaming Guild Member Level Filtering
questions.scenario:
Database: gaming_db | Collection: db.guilds | Field(s): guildId, members
A game admin wants to retrieve guilds with guildId 'GUILD_NA_01' where at least one member in the embedded members array has both role 'officer' and level greater than or equal to 80.
questions.explanation: The $elemMatch operator matches documents containing an array field with at least one element matching all specified criteria.
questions.misconception: Direct dot notation across array fields matches conditions across different array elements rather than a single unified element.

questions.title: Social Media Post Like Counter
questions.scenario:
Database: social_db | Collection: db.posts | Field(s): postId, likeCount
A service receives a batch of 5 new likes for a viral post identified by postId 'POST-8812'. Increment the likeCount field by 5 atomically.
questions.explanation: The $inc operator increments a numeric field by a specified value atomically without read-modify-write race conditions.
questions.misconception: Reading the current count and using $set introduces race conditions in high-concurrency environments.

questions.title: Flight Reservation Seat Lock Expiry Index
questions.scenario:
Database: airline_db | Collection: db.seat_holds | Field(s): heldAt, holdStatus
An airline reservation system temporarily holds seats for 15 minutes before checkout. Which index command correctly configures MongoDB to automatically purge documents 900 seconds after the 'heldAt' ISODate field?
questions.explanation: TTL indexes in MongoDB require the expireAfterSeconds option passed in the index specification object alongside a single date-indexed field.
questions.misconception: Assuming index options like expireAfterSeconds are included as keys inside the index key specification object instead of the options document.

questions.title: Restaurant Delivery Geospatial Proximity
questions.scenario:
Database: delivery_db | Collection: db.restaurants | Field(s): location, isOpen
A food delivery application queries for open restaurants within 3000 meters of a customer located at coordinates [-73.9857, 40.7484] (longitude, latitude).
options: db.restaurants.find({ isOpen: true, location: { $nearSphere: { $geometry: { type: 'Point', coordinates: [-73.9857, 40.7484] }, $maxDistance: 3000 } } })
db.restaurants.find({ isOpen: true, location: { $geoNear: { type: 'Point', coordinates: [-73.9857, 40.7484], distance: 3000 } } })
db.restaurants.find({ isOpen: true, location: { $near: { coordinates: [-73.9857, 40.7484], radius: 3000 } } })
questions.explanation: Using $nearSphere with a GeoJSON Point and $maxDistance (in meters) correctly calculates spherical proximity queries on 2dsphere indexes.
questions.misconception: Using legacy coordinate pairs with flat geometry radius operators rather than spherical distances measured in meters.

questions.title: Fintech Ledger Shard Key Monotonic Routing
questions.scenario:
Database: fintech_db | Collection: db.ledger_entries | Field(s): accountId, createdAt
You must configure a shard key to avoid monotonic insertion hotspots while maintaining targeted query routing for account audits.
questions.explanation: A compound hashed shard key starting with { accountId: 'hashed', createdAt: 1 } distributes writes across chunks via accountId while preserving range queries on createdAt for a given account.
questions.misconception: Developers often assume compound hashed shard keys must hash every field rather than just the prefix.

questions.title: IoT Telemetry Atomic Metric Windowing
questions.scenario:
Database: iot_db | Collection: db.device_metrics | Field(s): readings, currentBatch
Append a metric value 42.5 to the readings array only if currentBatch has not exceeded 100 entries, and atomically increment currentBatch.
questions.explanation: Combining the query predicate { currentBatch: { $lt: 100 } } with $push and $inc ensures conditional atomic progression in a single operation.
questions.misconception: Many assume conditional array updates require a multi-document transaction instead of a single query filter.

questions.title: E-Commerce Partial Unique Coupon Constraints
questions.scenario:
Database: ecommerce_db | Collection: db.coupons | Field(s): code, state
Enforce uniqueness on the 'code' field only for coupons where 'state' is equal to 'ACTIVE', ignoring EXPIRED or VOID codes.
questions.expectedCommand: db.coupons.createIndex({ code: 1 }, { unique: true, partialFilterExpression: { state: "ACTIVE" } })
acceptableAlternatives: db.coupons.createIndex({ code: 1 }, { partialFilterExpression: { state: "ACTIVE" }, unique: true })
db.coupons.createIndex({ code: 1 }, { unique: true, partialFilterExpression: { state: 'ACTIVE' } })
questions.explanation: A partial index with a partialFilterExpression enables the unique constraint to apply strictly to documents matching { state: 'ACTIVE' }.
questions.misconception: Sparse indexes are often mistakenly used, but sparse only checks field presence, not specific values.

questions.title: Aviation Flight Seat Map Array Filters
questions.scenario:
Database: aviation_db | Collection: db.flights | Field(s): seatMap, seatNumber, status
Update the status of seat '12A' inside the seatMap array to 'BOOKED' without replacing the entire document or other array items.
questions.explanation: The positional operator $ matches the first element in the seatMap array satisfying the query predicate, modifying only its status.
questions.misconception: Users frequently confuse the positional operator $ with the filtered positional operator $[<identifier>] when updating a single queried element.

questions.title: Hospital ICU Sensor Collation Constraints
questions.scenario:
Database: hospital_db | Collection: db.patient_alerts | Field(s): alertCode, severity
You need to query alertCode case-insensitively using an index created with collation { locale: 'en', strength: 2 }. What happens if you omit the collation in db.patient_alerts.find({ alertCode: 'code_red' })?
options: The query will perform a collection scan (COLLSCAN) because query collation must match index collation to use the index.
MongoDB automatically adopts the index's collation for the search and performs an IXSCAN case-insensitively.
The query throws a CollationMismatchException runtime error.
The query performs an IXSCAN using binary string comparison, ignoring the index's defined collation strength.
questions.explanation: Queries must explicitly specify the exact same collation as the index to be eligible to use that index; otherwise, MongoDB defaults to binary comparison and executes a collection scan.
questions.misconception: Engineers often assume that if an index exists with a specific collation, MongoDB infers and automatically applies it to standard queries.

questions.title: Fintech Ledger Reconciliation
questions.scenario:
Database: fintech_db | Collection: db.transactions | Field(s): ["metadata.audit_hash", "version"]
To prevent double-spending in a high-concurrency ledger, you must perform an atomic update that increments a 'version' counter only if the 'metadata.audit_hash' field is currently null or missing.
questions.explanation: Using $exists: false or equality to null allows targeting documents where the field is literally missing or unset before incrementing.
questions.misconception: Developers often forget that { field: null } matches both literal null and missing fields.

questions.title: IoT Telemetry Data Compression
questions.scenario:
Database: iot_db | Collection: db.sensor_readings | Field(s): ["timestamp", "reading"]
Which aggregation operator is most efficient for calculating the 'delta' between consecutive sensor readings within a specific time-series bucket using the bucket pattern?
questions.explanation: The $shift operator in the windowing stage allows access to the previous document's value to calculate differences without self-joins.
questions.misconception: Users often attempt complex $reduce logic on arrays instead of leveraging native window operators.

questions.title: Ad-Tech Clickstream Sharding
questions.scenario:
Database: adtech_db | Collection: db.clicks | Field(s): ["campaign_id", "ts"]
You are implementing a hashed sharding strategy to ensure even write distribution across 50 shards. Which command correctly enables sharding for this collection using a hashed campaign_id?
questions.explanation: Sharding a collection with a hashed key requires the shardCollection helper and specifying 'hashed' as the index type.
questions.misconception: Relying on monotonically increasing timestamps for shard keys leads to single-shard write bottlenecks.

questions.title: SaaS Multi-tenant Partial Indexing
questions.scenario:
Database: saas_platform | Collection: db.organizations | Field(s): ["tier", "org_id"]
To optimize storage for a system with 1 million 'free' tier tenants and only 5,000 'enterprise' tenants, you need an index on 'org_id' that ONLY indexes documents where 'tier' is exactly 'enterprise'.
questions.explanation: Partial indexes reduce index size and write overhead by only including documents that meet the specified filter criteria.
questions.misconception: Sparse indexes only check for field existence, whereas partial indexes allow specific value-based filtering.

questions.title: E-commerce Inventory Conflict Resolution
questions.scenario:
Database: ecommerce_db | Collection: db.inventory | Field(s): ["stock_levels", "sku"]
In a globally distributed database using a 'Cause-and-Effect' consistency model, which readConcern level ensures that a thread sees its own previous writes and maintains causal consistency?
questions.explanation: In MongoDB, readConcern 'majority' combined with causal consistency sessions ensures a node observes all changes that preceded it.
questions.misconception: Linearizable is often confused as the only way to see own writes, but it is much slower and more restrictive than necessary for causal consistency.

questions.title: Logistics Route Checkpoint Array Slice Update
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_db | Collection: db.shipments | Field(s): checkpoints, trackingNumber
A logistics platform stores movement logs in the checkpoints array. Append a new checkpoint document {"loc": "ORD", "ts": ISODate("2024-03-01T12:00:00Z")} to the checkpoints array for trackingNumber "TRK-9810", while keeping only the last 5 checkpoints sorted by ts in ascending order.
acceptableAlternatives: db.shipments.updateOne({ trackingNumber: 'TRK-9810' }, { $push: { checkpoints: { $each: [{ loc: 'ORD', ts: ISODate('2024-03-01T12:00:00Z') }], $sort: { ts: 1 }, $slice: -5 } } })
db.shipments.updateOne({ trackingNumber: "TRK-9810" }, { $push: { checkpoints: { $each: [{ loc: "ORD", ts: ISODate("2024-03-01T12:00:00Z") }], $slice: -5, $sort: { ts: 1 } } } })
questions.explanation: The $push modifier supports $each, $sort, and $slice combined to maintain a bounded, sorted embedded array atomically.
questions.misconception: Developers often believe $slice in $push can only truncate from the front with positive values, forgetting negative numbers keep trailing elements.

questions.title: Gaming Inventory Equipment Slot Bitwise Condition
questions.scenario:
Database: gaming_db | Collection: db.characters | Field(s): flags, characterId
In an MMORPG, character equip states are bitmasks stored in flags. Bit 3 (mask 8, 2^3) indicates an equipped off-hand shield. Find all characters that have bit 3 turned off (value 0 at position 3).
questions.explanation: $bitsAllClear matches documents where all specified bit positions (0-indexed array [3]) or bitmask values evaluate to 0.
questions.misconception: A common mistake is confusing 0-indexed bit positions ([3]) with decimal integer mask values (8).

questions.title: Social Platform Compound Multikey Index Bounds
questions.scenario:
Database: social_db | Collection: db.posts | Field(s): tags, mentions, publishedAt
A social networking service evaluates index creation over post metadata. Given an application requirement to query both the tags array and the mentions array in single read operations, why does creating the compound index { tags: 1, mentions: 1 } fail?
options: MongoDB enforces a restriction that a compound multikey index cannot contain more than one array field.
MongoDB requires multikey indexes containing strings to specify explicit collation rules before creation.
A compound index cannot combine two parallel array fields unless an explicit schema validator specifies fixed lengths.
Multikey indexes cannot be compound unless one of the keys is a unique primary identifier like _id.
questions.explanation: MongoDB restricts compound indexes from indexing more than one array field to prevent exponential index entry combinatorial explosions.
questions.misconception: Developers frequently assume MongoDB can cross-product two array fields in compound indexes without limits.

questions.title: Hospital Registry Encrypted Field Projection Exclusion
questions.scenario:
Database: hospital_db | Collection: db.admissions | Field(s): diagnosisCode, admissionDate, patientMRN
A clinical audit requires querying the admissions collection where admissionDate is greater than 2024-01-01, returning only diagnosisCode and excluding _id entirely.
questions.explanation: Field projections include required attributes with 1 and explicitly suppress the default _id field with _id: 0.
questions.misconception: Users often believe stating { diagnosisCode: 1 } automatically suppresses the _id field from being returned.

questions.title: Real Estate Listing Schema Validation Non-Enforcement
questions.scenario:
Database: realestate_db | Collection: db.properties | Field(s): price, propertyType
A collection has JSON Schema validation configured with validationLevel: 'moderate' and validationAction: 'error'. An existing document inserted prior to validation rule deployment has price: -100 (violating the schema). What happens when an update changes only the propertyType field to 'Condo'?
options: The update succeeds because 'moderate' validation only validates updates against existing documents that already complied with validation rules.
The update fails immediately with a DocumentValidationFailure error because the resulting document still contains invalid price.
The update succeeds with a warning logged to the mongod server log, but only if validationAction is configured to 'warn'.
The update fails because schema validation operates strictly at the document level regardless of the validationLevel setting.
questions.explanation: Under validationLevel: 'moderate', update checks apply only to existing documents that already matched the validation criteria prior to update.
questions.misconception: Developers assume 'moderate' validates all document updates unconditionally when validationAction is set to 'error'.

questions.title: Configuring Replica Set Connections
questions.scenario:
Database: fintech_db | Collection: db.transactions | Field(s): [transaction_id, status]
You are connecting to a production replica set via mongosh. To ensure your session only reads from secondary nodes to reduce load on the primary, which connection string option must you specify?
questions.explanation: The readPreference option determines how the driver directs read operations to the members of a replica set.
questions.misconception: Users often confuse readConcern (consistency) with readPreference (routing).

questions.title: Exporting Multi-tenant SaaS Data
questions.scenario:
Database: saas_platform | Collection: db.tenants | Field(s): [tenant_id, plan_type]
Use the command-line tool mongoexport to export all documents where 'plan_type' is 'Enterprise' into a JSON file named 'enterprise_clients.json'.
questions.explanation: mongoexport is a utility for exporting BSON data from a MongoDB instance to JSON or CSV formats.
questions.misconception: Learners often try to use mongodump for human-readable JSON, but mongodump produces binary BSON.

questions.title: Troubleshooting Connection Pools
questions.scenario:
Database: iot_telemetry | Collection: db.sensor_readings | Field(s): [sensor_id, ts]
Your Node.js application is hitting connection limits on the IoT database. Which parameter in the URI should you adjust to limit the maximum number of concurrent connections the driver maintains?
questions.explanation: maxPoolSize defines the maximum number of connections in the connection pool.
questions.misconception: Many believe MongoDB automatically handles unlimited connections without driver-side pooling limits.

questions.title: Restoring Production Backups
questions.scenario:
Database: healthcare_records | Collection: db.patients | Field(s): [patient_id, ssn]
You have a binary backup folder named 'dump'. Write the command to restore only the 'patients' collection to the 'healthcare_records' database using mongorestore.
questions.explanation: mongorestore handles BSON files created by mongodump and allows for targeted restoration of specific collections.
questions.misconception: Users often forget that mongorestore requires the path to the specific .bson file when restoring a single collection.

questions.title: Identifying Slow Gaming Queries
questions.scenario:
Database: gaming_logs | Collection: db.player_events | Field(s): [event_type, latency_ms]
You are using mongosh. Which command would you run to see the current operations that have been running for longer than 5 seconds in the gaming_logs database?
questions.explanation: db.currentOp() is a helper that wraps the currentOp administrative command to return in-progress operations.
questions.misconception: New users often look for slow queries in the logs before checking active operations via currentOp.

questions.title: Optimizing Multi-tenant SaaS Resource Attribution
questions.scenario:
Database: saas_infra | Collection: db.tenant_logs | Field(s): ["org_id", "resource_usage.cpu", "timestamp"]
You need to calculate the 95th percentile of CPU usage per organization across 100 million documents without exceeding the 100MB aggregation stage RAM limit, using a non-blocking approach.
options: Use { allowDiskUse: true } and the $percentile operator in a $group stage.
Implement a $facet stage to split processing into manageable chunks.
Utilize the $accumulator custom function to calculate a running t-digest percentile.
Index the timestamp and use a $bucket stage to reduce memory footprint.
questions.explanation: The $percentile operator (introduced in 7.0) or custom logic via $group requires allowDiskUse: true to handle datasets exceeding the 100MB RAM limit per stage.
questions.misconception: Users often forget that $push within $group can easily hit the 16MB document limit or stage RAM limits before the percentile calculation occurs.

questions.title: Logistics Route Geofencing with BigInt
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_v3 | Collection: db.vehicle_positions | Field(s): ["position", "route_id", "epoch_ns"]
Write a command to find all vehicles within a 500-meter radius of a specific Long/Lat coordinate, ensuring the query utilizes a geospatial index and filters for the most recent nanosecond epoch.
acceptableAlternatives: db.vehicle_positions.aggregate([{ $geoNear: { near: { type: "Point", coordinates: [-73.935, 40.730] }, distanceField: "dist", maxDistance: 500, spherical: true } }, { $sort: { epoch_ns: -1 } }])
questions.explanation: $nearSphere combined with a descending sort on a high-precision field like epoch_ns effectively retrieves the latest spatial event.
questions.misconception: Developers often use $geoWithin with $center, which uses radians, leading to incorrect distance calculations compared to $nearSphere's meter-based constraints.

questions.title: Healthcare HIPAA Audit Trail Sharding
questions.scenario:
Database: hospital_audit | Collection: db.access_logs | Field(s): ["patient_id", "provider_id", "log_id"]
To ensure data sovereignty and write scalability, you must choose a shard key strategy for a collection where 90% of queries filter by patient_id and log_id is a monotonically increasing Snowflake ID.
options: Ranged shard key on { patient_id: 1, log_id: 1 }
questions.explanation: A compound shard key starting with the most frequent query filter (patient_id) ensures query targeting, while log_id provides cardinality for chunk distribution.
questions.misconception: Choosing log_id alone as a ranged shard key creates a 'hot shard' bottleneck because all new writes will target the highest range shard.

questions.title: Gaming Leaderboard Atomic Level-Up
questions.scenario:
Database: gaming_platform | Collection: db.player_stats | Field(s): ["xp", "level", "inventory"]
Write a command to atomically increment 'xp' by 500 and, only if 'xp' exceeds 10000, set 'level' to 10 and add a 'veteran_badge' to the 'inventory' array.
questions.expectedCommand: db.player_stats.updateOne({ _id: "player1", xp: { $lt: 10000 } }, [{ $set: { xp: { $add: ["$xp", 500] } } }, { $set: { level: { $cond: { if: { $gte: ["$xp", 10000] }, then: 10, else: "$level" } }, inventory: { $cond: { if: { $gte: ["$xp", 10000] }, then: { $concatArrays: ["$inventory", ["veteran_badge"]] }, else: "$inventory" } } } }])
questions.explanation: Pipelined updates allow referencing the current field values within the update logic, enabling conditional complex logic in a single atomic operation.
questions.misconception: Many assume a standard $set and $inc can be combined with $cond without using the aggregation pipeline syntax [] in updateOne.

questions.title: Fintech Encryption-at-Rest Field Level Leakage
questions.scenario:
Database: banking_app | Collection: db.customers | Field(s): ["ssn", "pii_data", "key_id"]
When using Client-Side Field Level Encryption (CSFLE), which restriction applies to querying an encrypted field using 'random' encryption (not deterministic)?
options: You cannot perform equality matches or range queries on the field.
The field can only be queried using $text search.
Queries on the field must use the $expr operator.
The field must be indexed using a 2dsphere index.
questions.explanation: Randomized encryption results in different ciphertexts for the same plaintext, making equality matches and indexing for search impossible; only deterministic encryption allows equality matches.
questions.misconception: Users believe CSFLE handles all query types transparently, but encryption type (Random vs. Deterministic) strictly dictates query capabilities.

questions.title: Configuring Read Preference for High-Latency Global Fintech Nodes
questions.scenario:
Database: fintech_db | Collection: db.wire_transfers | Field(s): [transaction_id, metadata.latency_ms]
A multi-region global fintech cluster requires a query that prioritizes low-latency local reads but falls back to the nearest secondary if the local node is unavailable, ensuring the application doesn't block on primary elections.
questions.explanation: The 'nearest' read preference selects the member with the lowest network latency, regardless of its role (primary or secondary).
questions.misconception: Users often mistake 'primaryPreferred' for latency-based routing when it actually prioritizes the primary regardless of distance.

questions.title: Securing SaaS Multi-Tenancy with Connection String Options
questions.scenario:
Database: saas_platform | Collection: db.tenant_configs | Field(s): [tenant_id, auth_mechanism]
In a multi-tenant SaaS environment using X.509 certificates for authentication, which URI parameter is required to specify the location of the client certificate for the mongosh connection?
questions.explanation: The tlsCertificateKeyFile parameter in the connection string or mongosh flags specifies the path to the PEM file containing the certificate and key.
questions.misconception: Many assume the certificate is passed via a standard field like 'authSource', but X.509 requires external source handling and a specific key file path.

questions.title: Analyzing Replica Set Oplog Window for Healthcare Audit Logs
questions.scenario:
Database: hospital_db | Collection: db.audit_logs | Field(s): [op, ns, wall]
You are using 'mongodump' with the --oplog flag to ensure point-in-time consistency for a healthcare compliance backup. Which command allows you to check the current size and time window of the oplog to ensure it won't roll over during the dump?
questions.explanation: rs.printReplicationInfo() provides the oplog size and the time range covered, which is critical for ensuring backup consistency.
questions.misconception: Users often try rs.status(), which shows member state but doesn't explicitly calculate the time duration of the oplog window.

questions.title: Gaming Leaderboard Write Concern Strategies
questions.scenario:
Database: gaming_db | Collection: db.leaderboards | Field(s): [player_id, score, rank]
To ensure a score update is hardened to the majority of data-bearing nodes and written to the on-disk journal before returning success to the client, which writeConcern configuration must be used?
questions.explanation: w: 'majority' ensures data reaches most nodes, and j: true ensures the write is committed to the journal on those nodes.
questions.misconception: Developers often assume 'majority' implies journaling, but j: true must be specified to guarantee the write survives a process crash.

questions.title: Authentication database versus application database
questions.scenario:
Database: education_db | Collection: db.learners | Field(s): _id
The database user was created in admin but has read access to education_db. Which connection configuration correctly separates credential authentication from the application database?
options: Use authSource=admin and select education_db as the application database.
Use authSource=education_db regardless of where the user was created.
Move the password into the collection name.
questions.explanation: authSource identifies the database that holds the database user. The selected application database and assigned roles determine where authorized operations run.

questions.title: Selective Field Export for Healthcare Compliance
questions.scenario:
Database: hospital_db | Collection: db.patients | Field(s): [patient_id, blood_type]
You need to export only the non-sensitive fields 'patient_id' and 'blood_type' to a CSV file named 'report.csv' using the command line tools.
questions.explanation: mongoexport is the standard utility for producing CSV/JSON exports, and the --fields flag is mandatory when exporting to CSV to define the header.
questions.misconception: Attempting to use db.patients.find() for large-scale file exports instead of the native binary tools.

questions.title: SRV Record Connection Troubleshooting
questions.scenario:
Database: iot_db | Collection: db.sensors | Field(s): [deviceId, reading]
You are migrating an IoT telemetry backend to a sharded cluster using 'mongodb+srv://'. What is the primary functional difference this protocol provides compared to standard 'mongodb://'?
options: It enables TLS/SSL encryption by default for all data in transit.
It uses DNS seed lists to allow the client to discover all cluster nodes without updating the connection string when nodes change.
It automatically compresses sensor data using zlib before sending it to the database.
It allows the driver to perform automatic schema validation on the client side.
questions.explanation: The +srv protocol uses DNS SRV records to provide a list of available mongod instances, allowing for cluster membership changes without client-side config updates.
questions.misconception: Many assume +srv is purely for security/encryption, whereas its primary role is service discovery and simplified connection management.

questions.title: Partial Restore for SaaS Tenant Recovery
questions.scenario:
Database: saas_db | Collection: db.tenants | Field(s): [tenantId, plan]
A specific customer in a multi-tenant SaaS platform accidentally deleted their data. Use the command line to restore only the 'tenants' collection from a dump folder located at '/backups/yesterday/'.
questions.explanation: mongorestore allows for targeted recovery by specifying the database, collection, and the path to the specific BSON file.
questions.misconception: Running a full mongorestore on the root dump directory which would overwrite other tenants' data.

questions.title: Optimizing Connection Pool for Lambda Functions
questions.scenario:
Database: ecommerce_db | Collection: db.orders | Field(s): [orderDate, amount]
An e-commerce site uses AWS Lambda to process orders. Every invocation creates a new connection, exhausting the 'ecommerce_db' connection limit. What is the recommended strategy to manage connections in this serverless environment?
options: Increase the 'maxPoolSize' to 10000 in the Lambda connection string.
Call 'client.close()' at the very beginning of every Lambda function execution.
Define the MongoDB client variable outside the Lambda handler function to enable connection reuse across warm invocations.
Use the 'mongoimport' tool inside the Lambda to handle data insertion.
questions.explanation: In serverless architectures, defining the database client in the global scope allows the driver to reuse the connection pool during 'warm' starts, preventing connection exhaustion.
questions.misconception: Closing the connection at the end of every function (stateless approach) is often seen as 'clean' but causes massive overhead and potential connection storms.

questions.title: Querying High-Value Orders
questions.scenario:
Database: ecommerce_prod | Collection: db.orders | Field(s): ["total_amount", "status"]
Retrieve all documents from the orders collection where the status is 'shipped' and the total_amount is greater than 500.
questions.explanation: The $gt operator is used for greater-than comparisons within a find query object.
questions.misconception: Users often forget that multiple fields in a query object act as an implicit AND.

questions.title: Updating Patient Records
questions.scenario:
Database: healthcare_system | Collection: db.patients | Field(s): ["patient_id", "last_visit"]
Which command correctly updates a single patient with ID 'P-99' to set their last_visit date to the current timestamp?
questions.explanation: The updateOne method requires an update operator like $set to modify fields without overwriting the entire document.
questions.misconception: Omitting $set will replace the entire document with the new object in older shell methods or cause errors in newer ones.

questions.title: Deleting Inactive IoT Sensors
questions.scenario:
Database: smart_city_iot | Collection: db.sensors | Field(s): ["is_active"]
Remove all documents from the sensors collection where the is_active field is explicitly set to false.
questions.explanation: deleteMany is the standard method for removing multiple documents matching a specific filter.
questions.misconception: Users might use deleteOne which would only remove the first matching sensor instead of all inactive ones.

questions.title: Inserting New Fintech Account
questions.scenario:
Database: banking_app | Collection: db.accounts | Field(s): ["acc_type", "balance"]
What is the result of running: db.accounts.insertOne({ "acc_type": "savings", "balance": 1200 })?
options: A document is created and MongoDB automatically generates a unique _id field.
The command fails because an _id field was not explicitly provided.
A document is created but it will be inaccessible without a primary key.
The command creates a collection but does not insert the data yet.
questions.explanation: MongoDB automatically assigns a unique ObjectId to the _id field if it is not provided during insertion.
questions.misconception: Novices often assume the primary key must be manually defined like in some SQL configurations.

questions.title: Counting Game Sessions
questions.scenario:
Database: gaming_meta | Collection: db.sessions | Field(s): ["player_id"]
Write a command to count the total number of documents in the sessions collection.
questions.explanation: countDocuments({}) provides an accurate count of all documents in a collection matching the provided filter.
questions.misconception: Using count() is technically deprecated in some drivers in favor of the more explicit countDocuments() or estimatedDocumentCount().

questions.title: Bounded connection pool wait
questions.scenario:
Database: education_db | Collection: db.learners | Field(s): _id
All connections in an application pool are busy. New operations must fail rather than wait indefinitely for a free pooled connection. Which option specifically bounds that wait?
questions.explanation: waitQueueTimeoutMS bounds the time an operation waits to check out a connection from a busy pool. It is different from server selection and socket timeouts.

questions.title: Exporting Aggregated IoT Telemetry via mongoexport
questions.scenario:
Database: iot_db | Collection: db.sensors | Field(s): [reading, timestamp]
You must export only the documents where the 'reading' exceeds 100, formatted as a JSON array, using the command line tool. How do you specify the query and the output format?
questions.explanation: The --query flag accepts a JSON document for filtering, and --jsonArray ensures the output is a single valid JSON list rather than newline-delimited JSON.
questions.misconception: Thinking mongoexport supports full aggregation pipelines like $group; it only supports standard MQL queries.

questions.title: Analyzing Connection Pool Exhaustion in SaaS Environments
questions.scenario:
Database: saas_multi_tenant | Collection: db.tenants | Field(s): [tenantId, plan]
A multi-tenant application is hitting the 'maxPoolSize' limit under heavy load. You need to verify the current number of active vs available connections from the mongosh shell.
questions.explanation: The serverStatus command provides a 'connections' object showing current, available, and totalCreated connections.
questions.misconception: Users might try to check db.stats(), which provides storage info, not connection metrics.

questions.title: Server selection versus socket timeout
questions.scenario:
Database: education_db | Collection: db.learners | Field(s): _id
An application cannot find an eligible replica-set primary during an election. Which option bounds how long the driver searches for a suitable server?
questions.explanation: serverSelectionTimeoutMS bounds server selection. socketTimeoutMS addresses socket inactivity and does not replace a server-selection timeout.

questions.title: Partial Restore via mongorestore
questions.scenario:
Database: ecommerce_db | Collection: db.orders | Field(s): [orderDate, totalAmount]
An accidental deletion occurred. You have a full BSON dump directory 'dump/'. You need to restore only the 'orders' collection into the 'ecommerce_db' database without affecting other collections in that dump.
questions.explanation: Targeting the specific BSON file or using --nsInclude allows for granular restoration of a single collection.
questions.misconception: Running mongorestore on the root dump directory will attempt to restore all databases and collections unless scoped.

questions.title: Listing Databases in mongosh
questions.scenario:
Database: admin | Collection: db.system.version | Field(s): [version]
A DevOps engineer has established a connection to an IoT telemetry cluster and needs to quickly view all available databases on the server using the shell.
questions.explanation: In mongosh, the helper command 'show dbs' (or 'show databases') lists all databases along with their storage sizes.
questions.misconception: Learners often mix up SQL syntax like 'SHOW DATABASES;' or assume mongosh requires a JavaScript method like db.getDatabases().

questions.title: Switching Database Context
questions.scenario:
Database: ecommerce_db | Collection: db.products | Field(s): [sku, price]
A developer connects to an e-commerce cluster and wants to switch the working database context to 'ecommerce_db' to query catalog data.
questions.explanation: The 'use <database>' command switches the active database context in mongosh.
questions.misconception: Beginners often attempt to invoke a function like db.switchDatabase('ecommerce_db') instead of the built-in helper command.

questions.title: Default MongoDB Port in Connection Strings
questions.scenario:
Database: fintech_db | Collection: db.accounts | Field(s): [accountNumber, balance]
A software engineer is constructing a standard MongoDB URI to connect their local backend service to the fintech database instance.
questions.explanation: The default TCP port for a standalone mongod process is 27017.
questions.misconception: Users commonly confuse MongoDB's default port with standard relational ports like PostgreSQL (5432) or MySQL (3306).

questions.title: Checking Active Database Name
questions.scenario:
Database: hospital_db | Collection: db.patients | Field(s): [patientId, status]
A hospital database administrator wants to check the name of the currently selected database directly from the shell prompt.
questions.explanation: Executing 'db.getName()' or inspecting the identifier 'db' returns the name of the currently active database.
questions.misconception: Many users try to run 'SELECT DATABASE()' from relational SQL instead of using the mongosh 'db' object.

questions.title: Database Export CLI Utility
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_db | Collection: db.shipments | Field(s): [trackingCode, deliveryStatus]
A site reliability engineer needs to export shipments collection data into a JSON file from the host terminal without entering mongosh.
questions.explanation: 'mongoexport' is the MongoDB Command Line Database Tool used specifically to produce JSON or CSV exports of collection data.
questions.misconception: Learners frequently confuse 'mongodump' (binary BSON backups) with 'mongoexport' (human-readable JSON/CSV output).

questions.title: Configuring Change Stream Pre-Images for Auditing
questions.scenario:
Database: compliance_vault | Collection: db.fintech_transactions | Field(s): ["tx_status", "last_modified"]
To comply with financial regulations, you must ensure that change streams on the fintech_transactions collection return the full document before it was modified without performing an extra lookup. Which command enables this feature?
questions.explanation: The collMod command or createCollection option 'changeStreamPreAndPostImages' allows the cluster to store the previous version of a document in the oplog for change stream retrieval.
questions.misconception: Users often believe change streams provide the old data by default, but this requires explicit collection-level configuration.

questions.title: Optimizing WiredTiger Eviction for Gaming Telemetry
questions.scenario:
Database: gaming_platform | Collection: db.player_events | Field(s): ["event_type", "latency_ms"]
A high-throughput gaming database is experiencing 'cache pressure'. You need to adjust the WiredTiger storage engine configuration dynamically to trigger eviction earlier when the cache fills. Which command achieves this?
questions.explanation: The wiredTigerEngineRuntimeConfig parameter allows for tuning internal engine thresholds like eviction triggers without restarting the instance.
questions.misconception: Many administrators assume WiredTiger settings can only be set in the mongod.conf file at startup.

questions.title: Restricting Field-Level Access via mongosh Shell
questions.scenario:
Database: healthcare_records | Collection: db.patients | Field(s): ["ssn", "medical_history"]
You need to create a custom role 'limitedNurseRole' that allows querying the patients collection but explicitly forbids viewing the 'ssn' field by using Client-Side Field Level Encryption (CSFLE) or Queryable Encryption. Which helper defines the encrypted schema enforcement?
options: The 'validator' object within 'createCollection' using '$jsonSchema' and 'encrypt' keywords.
The 'db.collection.createIndex' command with the '{ hidden: true }' option.
questions.explanation: Server-side enforcement of encryption/masking for specific fields is defined via the $jsonSchema validator in the collection metadata.
questions.misconception: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) alone cannot hide specific fields within a document; it only controls collection-level actions.

questions.title: Connecting via mongosh with Tailable Cursors
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_tracker | Collection: db.truck_gps_capped | Field(s): ["coordinates", "timestamp"]
You are monitoring a capped collection of GPS data in real-time. Write a mongosh command that opens a tailable cursor which stays open after the initial data is exhausted.
questions.explanation: The .tailable() cursor method is specifically designed for capped collections to keep the connection alive for new incoming documents.
questions.misconception: Standard cursors close immediately when no more documents match; only tailable cursors wait for new data in capped collections.

questions.title: Analyzing Global Lock via mongotop
questions.scenario:
Database: saas_multi_tenant | Collection: db.tenant_logs | Field(s): ["tenant_id", "op_code"]
Your SaaS platform is experiencing latency. You suspect the 'tenant_logs' collection is consuming excessive write time. Which external tool command will show you the time spent by the database on read/write operations per collection every 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: mongotop provides a real-time view of the amount of time a MongoDB instance spends reading and writing data, broken down by collection.
questions.misconception: mongostat provides overall server metrics (ops/sec), while mongotop is required for collection-specific timing.

questions.title: Listing Collections in Logistics Database
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_hub | Collection: db.shipments | Field(s): trackingNumber, status
A logistics coordinator connected via mongosh wants to retrieve a list of all existing collection names within the active 'logistics_hub' database.
questions.explanation: Running 'show collections' (or 'show tables') outputs the list of collections in the current database.
questions.misconception: Learners often confuse 'show dbs' (which lists databases) with 'show collections' (which lists collections within the active database).

questions.title: Testing MongoDB Connection Ping
questions.scenario:
Database: healthcare_records | Collection: db.patients | Field(s): patientId, heartRate
A systems administrator wants to verify that the MongoDB server hosting patient telemetry is responsive by issuing a basic ping command via mongosh.
questions.explanation: The { ping: 1 } command issued through db.runCommand() verifies server availability and returns { ok: 1 }.
questions.misconception: Users often mistake application-level driver ping helper methods for built-in top-level mongosh commands.

questions.title: Determining mongosh Shell Version
questions.scenario:
Database: fintech_ledger | Collection: db.transactions | Field(s): txId, amount
A financial audit team requires documentation of the exact mongosh client version being used to query high-value transactions. Which command displays the shell version?
questions.explanation: In mongosh, version() returns the client shell version, whereas db.version() returns the MongoDB server version.
questions.misconception: Developers frequently run db.version(), which checks the database engine rather than the mongosh CLI tool itself.

questions.title: Importing Sensor Telemetry with mongoimport
questions.scenario:
Database: iot_telemetry | Collection: db.readings | Field(s): deviceId, temperature
A DevOps engineer needs to import a newline-delimited JSON file named 'data.json' directly into the 'readings' collection within the 'iot_telemetry' database from their terminal shell. Which command accomplishes this?
questions.explanation: mongoimport is the official command-line utility used to ingest JSON, CSV, or TSV data into MongoDB collections.
questions.misconception: Novices frequently confuse mongorestore (designed for binary BSON dumps produced by mongodump) with mongoimport (designed for text JSON/CSV).

questions.title: Viewing Server Connection Statistics
questions.scenario:
Database: gaming_meta | Collection: db.players | Field(s): playerId, currentScore
A backend engineer suspects client connection leaks and wants to inspect total active and available client connections on the server using mongosh.
questions.explanation: The connections subdocument of db.serverStatus() reports 'current', 'available', and 'totalCreated' connection metrics.
questions.misconception: Learners often look for a 'db.connections()' helper function that does not exist instead of inspecting db.serverStatus().

questions.title: Configuring Max Staleness for Global IoT Reads
questions.scenario:
Database: telemetry_hub | Collection: db.sensor_logs | Field(s): [metadata, ts]
To minimize cross-region latency in a globally distributed IoT environment, you must configure a connection string that allows reads from secondaries only if they are no more than 90 seconds behind the primary.
questions.explanation: The maxStalenessSeconds option is used with secondary read preferences to specify the maximum allowable replication lag for a secondary to be eligible for reads.
questions.misconception: Developers often confuse maxStalenessSeconds with secondaryAcceptableLatencyMS, which controls local threshold selection rather than replication lag.

questions.title: Optimizing WiredTiger Cache for SaaS Multi-tenancy
questions.scenario:
Database: saas_platform | Collection: db.tenant_data | Field(s): [tenantId, payload]
You are using mongostat to diagnose a performance dip. Which metric in the output indicates that the WiredTiger cache is full and the eviction server cannot keep up with the incoming write load?
options: The 'qr' (queue read) column showing high values
The 'ar' (active read) column reaching the connection limit
questions.explanation: High 'dirty %' in WiredTiger indicates that many pages are modified in memory but not yet persisted, triggering aggressive eviction which can throttle application throughput.
questions.misconception: It is often wrongly assumed that virtual memory size (vsize) is the primary indicator of cache pressure in MongoDB.

questions.title: Restoring specific collection with mongorestore
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_app | Collection: db.shipments | Field(s): [trackingId, status]
You have a full BSON dump directory named 'dump/'. Write the command to restore ONLY the 'shipments' collection into the 'logistics_app' database using 4 parallel threads.
questions.explanation: The mongorestore utility uses --db and --collection to target specific namespaces, and -j or --numParallelCollections to increase throughput.
questions.misconception: Users often forget that specifying a collection requires pointing the path directly to the specific .bson file or using --nsInclude.

questions.title: Analyzing Index Usage with mongosh
questions.scenario:
Database: retail_analytics | Collection: db.inventory_snapshots | Field(s): [sku, warehouseId]
You need to identify which indexes in the 'inventory_snapshots' collection have not been utilized since the last server restart to prune redundant indexes.
questions.explanation: The $indexStats aggregation stage provides statistics regarding the use of each index in a collection, including the 'accesses' count.
questions.misconception: Many users believe db.collection.getIndexes() provides usage statistics, but it only returns index definitions.

questions.title: Securing X.509 Authentication for Fintech Microservices
questions.scenario:
Database: fintech_core | Collection: db.ledger_entries | Field(s): [txn_id, amount]
When connecting to a cluster using X.509 client certificate authentication via mongosh, which parameter must be set to the specific Subject Name of the certificate as the user?
questions.explanation: MongoDB X.509 authentication requires the mechanism to be specified and the user must be defined in the '$external' virtual database.
questions.misconception: It is a common mistake to try and authenticate X.509 users against the 'admin' or local database, which will fail.

questions.title: Configuring SRV Polling for Dynamic Cluster Scaling
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_fleet | Collection: db.telemetry_nodes | Field(s): [connection_string, heartbeats]
An expert SRE needs to migrate a high-throughput fleet tracking system to a MongoDB Atlas sharded cluster. To ensure the client drivers automatically discover new mongos instances as they are added to the tier without restarting the application service, which connection string component and DNS configuration must be utilized?
options: The mongodb+srv:// protocol using a single DNS SRV record and TXT records for options.
The mongodb:// protocol with a comma-separated list of all shards and the replicaSet parameter.
A standard A record pointing to a Load Balancer that distributes traffic to the mongos processes.
The use of the connect=direct parameter in the connection string to force discovery of new nodes.
questions.explanation: The mongodb+srv connection format allows drivers to query DNS for SRV records, enabling the cluster to update its node list (mongos or replica set members) dynamically without client-side configuration changes.
questions.misconception: One might assume a standard Load Balancer is preferred, but this breaks the driver's ability to maintain server-side session affinity and monitor topology changes directly.

questions.title: Update Array Element by Condition
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_db | Collection: db.shipments | Field(s): trackingHistory, status
Update the status of the specific tracking history entry with code 'ARRIVED_HUB' to 'PROCESSED' for shipment with _id 101.
questions.explanation: The positional operator '$' acts as a placeholder for the first array element matching the query criteria.
questions.misconception: Developers often try to update array elements directly using their index or mistakenly use the all-positional operator '$[]' instead of '$'.

questions.title: Find With Element Match
questions.scenario:
Database: hospital_db | Collection: db.patients | Field(s): vitals, systolic, diastolic
Which query retrieves patients who have at least one vitals log where systolic is greater than 140 AND diastolic is greater than 90?
questions.explanation: $elemMatch ensures that multiple field criteria are satisfied by the exact same array element rather than across different elements in the array.
questions.misconception: Using direct dot notation on arrays can cause false positives where criteria are met across distinct sub-documents in the array.

questions.title: Increment Counter with Condition
questions.scenario:
Database: gaming_db | Collection: db.player_stats | Field(s): userId, score, level
Atomically increment the 'score' field by 250 for player with userId 'u8912' and set 'level' to 5.
questions.explanation: $inc handles numeric increments while $set updates fixed values, and both can be executed within a single update document.
questions.misconception: Developers sometimes mistakenly write two consecutive update commands or attempt to read the score first and calculate the increment client-side.

questions.title: Conditional Upsert Query
questions.scenario:
Database: iot_db | Collection: db.device_readings | Field(s): deviceId, timestamp, reading
Consider the command: db.device_readings.updateOne({ deviceId: 'dev_A1', timestamp: ISODate('2023-10-01T00:00:00Z') }, { $setOnInsert: { reading: 0 }, $set: { lastChecked: new Date() } }, { upsert: true }). If no matching document exists, what does $setOnInsert do?
options: It applies { reading: 0 } only if the document is being inserted as a new document.
It sets { reading: 0 } regardless of whether the document already exists or is inserted.
It raises a validation error if the field 'reading' is not present in the matching document.
It overwrites the 'reading' field if the document exists, but ignores it during an insert.
questions.explanation: $setOnInsert assigns values to the target fields only during an insert operation triggered by an upsert; it is ignored if an existing document is updated.
questions.misconception: Users often confuse $setOnInsert with a default field constraint that applies during every update cycle.

questions.title: Delete Multiple Documents by Criteria
questions.scenario:
Database: fintech_db | Collection: db.fraud_alerts | Field(s): resolved, createdAt
Delete all resolved fraud alerts created before January 1, 2023.
acceptableAlternatives: db.fraud_alerts.deleteMany({ resolved: true, createdAt: { $lt: new Date("2023-01-01T00:00:00Z") } })
questions.explanation: deleteMany() removes all documents matching the specified filter including Boolean and date-range conditions.
questions.misconception: Using remove() without multi: true or calling deleteOne() will only delete a single document instead of the entire qualifying dataset.

questions.title: Atomic State Transition with Conditional Update
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_db | Collection: db.shipments | Field(s): ["status", "location_history", "last_updated"]
Update a shipment's status to 'DELIVERED' and push the final location to the history array, but only if the current status is exactly 'IN_TRANSIT'.
questions.codeSnippet: db.shipments.updateOne({ _id: 101, status: "IN_TRANSIT" }, { $set: { status: "DELIVERED", last_updated: new Date() }, $push: { location_history: "Chicago Hub" } });
questions.explanation: This requires a query filter for the current status and the use of both $set and $push operators within a single update call.
questions.misconception: Users often forget that you can combine different update operators ($set and $push) in a single atomic operation.

questions.title: Projecting Computed Metadata in Search
questions.scenario:
Database: saas_db | Collection: db.tenants | Field(s): ["subscription_level", "active_users"]
Retrieve all tenants with a 'Premium' subscription, but return only the 'tenant_id' and the size of the 'active_users' array using a modern aggregation-style projection.
questions.explanation: Starting in MongoDB 4.4, find() projections support aggregation expressions like $size.
questions.misconception: Many developers think $size can only be used in the $match stage or via the aggregation pipeline.

questions.title: Bulk Insertion with Ordered Constraint
questions.scenario:
Database: iot_db | Collection: db.telemetry | Field(s): ["sensor_id", "ts", "val"]
Insert three documents representing sensor readings. Ensure that if the second document fails a validation/duplicate key error, the third document is NOT inserted.
questions.expectedCommand: db.telemetry.insertMany([{sensor_id:1, ts:10, val:5}, {sensor_id:2, ts:11, val:6}, {sensor_id:3, ts:12, val:7}], { ordered: true })
acceptableAlternatives: db.telemetry.insertMany([{sensor_id:1, ts:10, val:5}, {sensor_id:2, ts:11, val:6}, {sensor_id:3, ts:12, val:7}])
questions.explanation: The 'ordered' parameter defaults to true, which stops execution on the first error encountered during a bulk insert.
questions.misconception: Users often confuse ordered inserts with transactions; while ordered stops on error, previous successful inserts are not rolled back.

questions.title: Finding Missing Fields in Healthcare Records
questions.scenario:
Database: hospital_db | Collection: db.patients | Field(s): ["insurance_provider", "policy_number"]
Identify all patient records that are missing the 'insurance_provider' field entirely or have it explicitly set to null.
questions.explanation: Querying for { field: null } matches documents where the field is null and documents where the field does not exist.
questions.misconception: It is a common mistake to think $exists: false is required to find null values, but the direct null equality covers both cases.

questions.title: Renaming Fields Across Multi-tenant Data
questions.scenario:
Database: fintech_db | Collection: db.accounts | Field(s): ["balance", "available_funds"]
Rename the field 'balance' to 'available_funds' for all documents where the 'currency' is 'USD'.
questions.explanation: The $rename operator moves the value from the old field name to the new field name atomically.
questions.misconception: Newer users sometimes try to use $set with the old field value, which is not atomic and harder to write.

questions.title: Logistics Dispatch Update
questions.scenario:
Database: logistics_hub | Collection: db.deliveries | Field(s): [trackingId, status]
Update the status of a specific delivery to 'shipped' using its unique tracking ID 'TRK-9902'.
questions.explanation: The updateOne method with the $set operator is the standard way to modify a single field in a specific document.
questions.misconception: Using update without $set would replace the entire document instead of just the status field.

questions.title: SaaS Subscription Lookup
questions.scenario:
Database: saas_platform | Collection: db.subscriptions | Field(s): [planType, isActive]
Find all active subscriptions that are currently on the 'Enterprise' plan.
questions.explanation: In MongoDB, query criteria are passed as an object to the find method where multiple fields imply a logical AND.
questions.misconception: Assuming SQL-like syntax or separate method chaining for simple filtering.

questions.title: Healthcare Record Insertion
questions.scenario:
Database: health_portal | Collection: db.vitals | Field(s): [patientId, heartRate]
Add a new vitals reading for patient 'P-505' with a heartRate of 72.
questions.explanation: The insertOne method adds a single document into the specified collection.
questions.misconception: Attempting to use a save method which is deprecated in modern MongoDB drivers.

questions.title: Social Media Engagement Cleanup
